newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen down after quiet, range-bound trade.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen down after quiet, range-bound trade.

text.p: The benchmark three-month December euroyen futures contract ended a range-bound, quiet morning at its day's low after book-squaring emerged in the wake of stronger stocks and a rise in the dollar.

The Bank of Japan's (BOJ) morning market operation, which drained 100 billion yen from the market and left the market in surplus by 200 billion yen, compared with Wednesday's 300 billion yen, also weighed the topside slightly, they said.
The key December contract ended the morning at 99.02, its day's low, after rising as high as 99.08, with turnover of 29,346 contracts. Wednesday's Tokyo settlement was 99.05.
"Virtually all of Wednesday's buying factors have now disappeared, leaving the market vulnerable to some technical-linked book-squaring," one city bank trader said.

Euroyen futures rose strongly Wednesday on a combination of weak stocks, a strong yen and an accomodative BOJ operation, as expectations spread in the market that the central bank is unlikely to raise interest rates in the coming months.

But while December managed to hang onto part of these gains, the topside was growing heavy from around 99.05-06, where sales are lining up, the city bank trader added. A dearth of fresh factors made activity lacklustre.
December rose to 99.08 in overnight trade, and started Thursday Tokyo trade strong as a result, rising to the day's high shortly after trade began, the city bank dealer said.

But unexpected strength in Tokyo stocks, combined with the BOJ operation and the dollar's rise above 112 yen, soon took it down, with afternoon trade possibly seeing it drift as low as 99.00, he added. The Nikkei ended the morning up by 216.82.

In the interbank market, overnight call money was traded at 0.46 percent against Wednesday's 0.47 percent. Traders said that many in the market seem to have already taken what funds they need before the current bank reporting period ends Friday.
In the longer end of the market, around 10 billion yen of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.59 percent, down from Wednesday's 0.60 percent.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, three-year IRS rates were quoted at 1.51/1.58 percent, up from 1.48/1.52 percent Wednesday.
